$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $v$ shown above. Which of the following statements are true?

- $v$ is an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =4$ of $A$
- $v$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $3$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =4$ of $A$
- $v$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $2$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =4$ of $A$

feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14097559/assets/df5848bfb08f41036e8ef295a61023eefda252d0f0c32cd7fc64ec1f0b0d5c0b.png)

 

Notice the following properties of the given slope field:

- First, the slopes become vertical as $y\to -3$ only. 

Of the given equations, the only equations that satisfy this condition are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{1}{y+3} \\ {y}^{′} & =-\frac{1}{(y+3)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

- Second, the line $y=-3$ divides the plane into $2$ regions. The sign of the slopes in each of the $2$ regions are easily deduced by considering the behavior of the solution curves in these regions. This information is summarized in the following table:

| Region | $y<-3$ | $y>-3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Slope | $↘$ | $↗$ |
| Sign | $-$ | $+$ |

Of the two remaining options, the only one that gives this behavior is

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{1}{y+3}.
$$
